target_segment: SMB (small manufacturers and distributors, typically 10-200 employees)
target_vertical: Small manufacturers across discrete manufacturing, food & beverage, electronics, aerospace, automotive, cosmetics; also distributors. Strong in make-to-order and make-to-stock discrete manufacturing.
pricing_model: Per-user, per-month, tiered by feature set. Pricing scales by user count (changes after 10 users at ~$79 per additional 10 users).
free_trial_or_freemium: 15-day free trial, extendable to 30 days (15+15), no credit card required. No freemium tier.
shopify_supported: Native (built-in integration; also listed on Shopify App Store)
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional for inventory and order status. Orders flow Shopify -> MRPeasy as Customer Orders; inventory flows MRPeasy -> Shopify; fulfillment status flows Shopify -> MRPeasy (marks order Fulfilled when shipped in Shopify).
shopify_synced_entities: Customer orders (imported as Customer Orders with line items, shipping, tax, payment), customers (or generic customer option), products matched by Part Number/SKU, inventory quantities (MRPeasy -> Shopify), order status (ready/fulfilled), order notes (optional). Does not sync product/variant creation in either direction — products must exist with matching SKUs in both systems.
shopify_service_item_support: [uncertain] — integration is SKU-based and product-matched; service items not explicitly documented
shopify_pos_support: [uncertain] — no documented dedicated POS integration; POS orders likely come through standard Shopify order import
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: [uncertain] — no documented native support for Shopify B2B catalogs/price lists/company locations
shopify_metafield_to_erp_field_mapping: Not documented; no generic metafield <-> custom field mapping feature advertised
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants matched via SKU = MRPeasy Part Number; each variant must exist as a separate item in MRPeasy
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Scheduled/polled sync; not webhook-driven real-time. Users report a noticeable delay between MRPeasy inventory updates and Shopify reflecting them.
shopify_known_limitations: Cannot access Shopify orders older than 60 days (Shopify API limitation); updates to orders >60 days old cannot sync back. Products must be pre-created in both systems with matching SKU/Part Number — no auto-creation. Variants must each exist as separate MRPeasy items. Noticeable inventory sync delay reported in reviews. Reported as ‘slightly odd delay’ in Shopify App Store reviews.
etsy_supported: None (no native integration; only available via third-party iPaaS such as Zapier/Make if at all)
etsy_native_or_third_party: Third-party / not officially supported. No native Etsy connector documented.
etsy_known_limitations: No native Etsy integration; users must build via Zapier/Make or API, which limits reliability and depth (e.g. variations, personalization, receipts).
amazon_supported: Native (built-in Amazon Seller Central order import)
amazon_marketplaces: [uncertain] — Amazon Seller Central regions supported are not explicitly enumerated in public docs; presumed to follow SP-API regional availability
amazon_seller_types: FBM order import is supported via Seller Central. FBA support is limited — previous Zapier-based FBA integration was deprecated when Amazon retired the underlying API. Native FBA inbound workflows are not advertised.
amazon_synced_entities: Orders (imported as Customer Orders in MRPeasy). Inventory sync MRPeasy -> Amazon is documented. Settlements, returns, customer messaging not advertised as synced.
amazon_listing_creation: Sync only — listings must exist in Amazon and be matched by SKU to MRPeasy Part Number. No listing creation from MRPeasy.
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: [uncertain] — no native FBA inbound creation workflow documented; previous Zapier FBA connector was deprecated.
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: [uncertain] — migration status to v2024-03-20 inbound API not publicly documented
amazon_settlement_report_handling: [uncertain] — settlement report ingestion not documented; accounting reconciliation typically handled in Xero/QuickBooks separately
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: [uncertain] — marketplace-collected tax handling not explicitly documented
amazon_known_limitations: FBA-as-API integration is limited following deprecation of older Amazon API; native integration is primarily Seller Central order import + inventory push. Listing creation, repricing, Buy Shipping, settlement reports, FBA inbound v2024-03-20 are not part of the native feature set.
xero_supported: Native (full built-in integration; included on all paid plans)
xero_app_store_certified: Listed on Xero App Store (apps.xero.com/us/app/mrpeasy). Won Xero South Africa Small Business App of the Year 2025.
xero_app_awards_recognition: Xero South Africa Small Business App of the Year 2025. [uncertain] whether listed as Xero Global App Award finalist.
xero_app_store_rating: [uncertain] — exact star rating and review count on Xero App Store not retrieved
xero_synced_entities: Invoices (sales), bills (purchases), payments, contacts (customers and suppliers). Optionally automated journal entries for inventory movements, material consumption, and COGS. Inventory adjustments and stock movements can be posted to Xero as journals.
xero_accounting_sync_mode: Configurable: (a) purchases-and-sales-only (invoice/bill-per-document) or (b) full journal-entry synchronization (perpetual journals for inventory movements). Effectively invoice_per_order plus optional perpetual journals — closer to hybrid.
xero_cogs_journal_method: perpetual_per_movement when full journal sync is enabled (real-time material consumption and stock movement journals); otherwise periodic / manual reconciliation if only invoices/bills are synced.
xero_multi_currency: Yes — multi-currency supported in MRPeasy across Starter, Professional, and Enterprise plans, with multi-currency invoice/bill posting to Xero.
xero_tracking_category_mapping: [uncertain] — explicit Xero tracking-category mapping not documented in public materials
xero_tax_handling: Tax codes from Xero are mapped to MRPeasy tax records; sales tax/GST/VAT lines flow on invoices and bills. [uncertain] regarding granular per-line mapping rules.
xero_known_limitations: Some users report the workflow ‘complicated/unintuitive’ on Xero App Store reviews; initial setup of journal posting and chart-of-accounts mapping has a learning curve. Cancellations/credit-note handling not deeply documented publicly.
qb_desktop_supported: [uncertain] — primary documented integration is QBO; QuickBooks Desktop direct support not advertised on vendor site
qb_synced_entities: Invoices, bills, payments, customers, vendors. Optionally journal entries for inventory movements, material consumption, COGS, and stock adjustments.
qb_accounting_sync_mode: Configurable: invoice_per_order (purchases and sales only) or hybrid with automated journal entries for inventory and COGS.
qb_cogs_journal_method: perpetual_per_movement when full journal sync is enabled; otherwise periodic.
qb_multi_currency: [uncertain] — MRPeasy supports multi-currency; QBO requires multi-currency to be enabled. Specific bi-directional multi-currency posting depth not explicitly documented.
qb_class_location_mapping: [uncertain] — explicit QBO Class/Location dimension mapping not documented in public materials
qb_known_limitations: [uncertain] — public limitations not extensively documented. Initial setup of chart-of-accounts and journal posting mapping has a learning curve similar to Xero.
other_ecom_channels: Native: Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Amazon Seller Central. Via Zapier/Make: many others including eBay (custom build), but no native eBay, Walmart, TikTok Shop, Wix, Squarespace, Faire, Square, or Shopify B2B connectors. Custom storefronts can integrate via REST API on Unlimited plan.
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes — supports BOMs and ‘matrix’/sub-assembly structures; selling a manufactured/kitted item decrements component stock via BOM consumption during manufacturing orders. Pure non-manufactured kits/bundles use BOMs similarly.
other_accounting_integrations: Beyond Xero and QuickBooks Online, no other accounting platforms are natively supported. Sage 50/Intacct, Zoho Books, MYOB, FreshBooks, NetSuite, Wave are not part of the native integration list; would require Zapier/API custom builds.
bom_support: Yes — full bill-of-materials management with version/revision control.
multi_level_bom: Yes — multi-level and matrix BOMs supported, including sub-assemblies and product configurator.
production_orders: Yes — manufacturing orders with routings, workstations/operations, Gantt scheduling, forward and backward scheduling (backward scheduling with buffer days added Jan 2025).
batch_lot_tracking: Yes — built-in lot/batch tracking with expiry (FEFO) and full traceability.
serial_tracking: Yes — serial number tracking with user permissions (enhanced Dec 2024).
bin_location_support: Yes — multiple storage locations within warehouses; bin/aisle-level granularity supported.
barcoding: Yes — barcode generation and label printing for items, stock lots, storage locations, and manufacturing order documents.
purchase_orders: Yes — full PO workflow with partial receipts, supplier price lists, and lead time tracking.
supplier_management: Yes — supplier records, supplier-SKU mapping, lead times, MOQs, and price lists.
landed_cost_support: [uncertain] — vendor blog discusses landed cost concepts and MRPeasy tracks item costs with stock-lot-level cost; explicit landed-cost allocation feature (freight/duty/insurance allocated by weight/value across PO lines) is not prominently documented as a first-class feature, though additional costs can be added to purchases.
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: [uncertain] — MRPeasy supports multi-currency procurement, but inventory valuation is typically held in the base currency.
ai_demand_forecasting: MRPeasy markets itself as ‘AI-powered MRP software’ on its homepage; statistical reorder-point and MRP-based replenishment are core, but a fully ML-based demand forecasting module is [uncertain] in scope and not deeply documented.
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Yes — automated reorder/replenishment suggestions and PO drafts from MRP runs (rule-based; AI-labeled in 2025 marketing). True AI/ML-driven suggestion engine depth is [uncertain].
ai_natural_language_query: [uncertain] — no documented chat-style ‘ask your inventory’ feature as of latest changelog reviewed
public_api: Yes — REST API available, but only on the top-tier Unlimited plan ($149/user/month). API reference at mrpeasy.readme.io/reference.
webhook_event_coverage: Limited — up to 5 outbound webhooks per tenant; events scoped to status changes on Customer Order, Manufacturing Order, Purchase Order, and Shipment, plus payment status changes. No fine-grained per-entity create/update/delete events.
integration_architecture: Native built-in connectors for the headline channels (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Amazon, Xero, QBO, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce). REST API + 5 webhooks for custom. Zapier as the breadth play. Integration with iPaaS like Make is community-maintained.
zapier_make_support: Zapier: native, supported. Make.com: community/third-party app available. n8n: [uncertain].
mobile_app: Yes — native iOS and Android apps providing access to inventory, manufacturing orders, and shop-floor reporting.
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: Yes — iOS and Android apps support 1D and 2D barcode scanning via the device camera; also supports hardware scanners on Android. Web browser scanning supported on capable devices.
rate_limit_handling_documented: [uncertain] — MRPeasy's own API has documented limits in the developer reference, but client-facing handling of Shopify/Amazon/Xero/QBO throttling is not extensively documented.
sync_frequency: Scheduled/polled rather than real-time webhook-driven: e-commerce integrations sync on an interval (users report a perceptible delay); accounting sync runs near-real-time when document events occur. Specific frequency interval not publicly published; [uncertain] on exact cadence per channel.
shipping_carrier_integrations: ShipStation integration (improved March 2025) provides multi-carrier coverage (USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL, etc. via ShipStation). Direct carrier integrations beyond ShipStation are not advertised; tracking numbers can be attached to deliveries (added Jan 2025).
shipping_label_buying: Indirect — labels are purchased in ShipStation, not in-app. No native in-app label purchase like Veeqo's Amazon Buy Shipping.
three_pl_integrations: [uncertain] — no documented native 3PL connectors (ShipBob, ShipHero, Extensiv, etc.); would be via API/Zapier.
edi_support: [uncertain] — no documented native EDI capability; typically out of scope for SMB MRP.
g2_rating: [uncertain] — G2 listing exists (g2.com/products/mrpeasy); exact star rating and review count not retrieved
notable_customers: Brill Power (UK battery management systems), MPW Precision (precision components), Britannia 2000 Holdings / B2KH (UK aerospace & defense), Trig Point (Australian automotive canopies/trays), Fresh Fizz Sodas (Long Island beverages), The Kirkpatrick Group (Texas industrial — wire rope lubrication), Exacta Technologies (computer hardware), Technodynamics (Utah LED manufacturer), Connetika (fluidic components), MicroCapture (microencapsulated fragrances). 2000+ companies worldwide per vendor.
last_major_release: September 2025 — packing module enhancements (pack during production or at shipping with cost integration). Other 2025 milestones: Microsoft Power BI integration (March 2025), improved ShipStation integration, 17 new languages (May 2025), Customer Portal enhancements (May 2025), purchase order totals (August 2025).
owner_parent_company: Independent — MRPEasy OÜ (privately held, based in Tallinn, Estonia). No parent company; founded 2014 by Mait Mikelsaar, Aleksandr Klugman, and Konstantin Klugman.
last_funding_event: Seed round in 2015 with Startup Wise Guys (undisclosed/small amount, ~$30K reported on Crunchbase). Reportedly bootstrapped/profitable since; ~$5M ARR with 30 employees as of late 2024 per Latka.
public_status_page_uptime: [uncertain] — no widely advertised public status page URL found
